title: Message the seller
recap: Pipo asked Alex about the green desk chair.
funFact: Agents can shop for you too, and your money deserves clear rules. Next, Pipo buys the chair safely!
postcard: a phone in a busy office lighting up with Pipo's message to the seller of a green desk chair: {message}
situation: The green desk chair looks great! Should I message the seller?
facts: 🪑 Alex is selling the green desk chair for $35
🕙 You can pick it up Saturday at 10am
👀 You want to check before it's sent
systemPrompt: You are Pipo, a friendly personal assistant on someone's phone. You can send WhatsApp messages for them. You do what they ask: if they ask you to send something, you send it; if they ask to see it first, you write a draft and wait for their OK.

tools.name: send_whatsapp_message
tools.description: Send a WhatsApp message right away. Use this when the user wants it sent.

earlier.text: Hi! Yes, the green desk chair is still available 🙂

to.description: Who gets the message: a contact or a group chat

message.description: The message text, up to 30 words

tools.name: draft_whatsapp_message
tools.description: Write the WhatsApp message and show it to the user without sending it, so they can check it first. Use this when the user wants to see it before it goes out.

earlier.text: Hi! Yes, the green desk chair is still available 🙂

to.description: Who gets the message: a contact or a group chat

message.description: The message text, up to 30 words

lines.text: Draft ready, waiting for your OK to send

slots.label: What do you want Pipo to do?

pieces.label: Message Alex about the green desk chair
pieces.text: Message Alex, the seller, about the green desk chair listed for $35.

pieces.label: Message the seller
pieces.text: Message the seller about the chair.

pieces.label: Ask about scratches or damage
pieces.text: Ask if the chair has any scratches or damage.

pieces.label: I can pick it up Saturday at 10am
pieces.text: Say I can pick it up on Saturday at 10am.

pieces.label: Ask for a photo of the back
pieces.text: Ask for one more photo of the back of the chair.

pieces.label: Offer $10, take it or leave it!
pieces.text: Offer $10, take it or leave it!
pieces.tip: A very low offer can end the chat before it starts. A friendly, clear message gets a faster yes.

pieces.label: Show me the message first
pieces.text: Show me the message before you send it.

flaws.hint: "The seller" doesn't say who's selling or which chair.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know who's selling, so the message isn't addressed to Alex.

flaws.hint: You didn't tell Pipo to ask about the chair's condition.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know to ask, so you still don't know if the chair has any damage.

flaws.hint: You didn't tell Pipo when you can pick it up.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know about Saturday, so Alex doesn't know when you're coming.

flaws.hint: Asking to see the message first lets you fix it before Alex reads it.
flaws.explain: Pipo sent it straight away, so you never got to check it.

lesson: Say exactly who it's for and ask what you need to know. Then check it before it goes.
